thread:
aaron: Quick sync — thinking about switching from global kernel selector to arch-scoped kernel-priority lists + sequence-length bins. Keeps fast paths narrower and reduces lookup cost.

maria: Curious how that affects cache keying for KV/prefix cache. Do we need separate materialized caches per seq-bin?

aaron: My proposal: KV cache remains per model variant + device, but we add a seq_bin tag to entries for fast lookup. Not duplicate the full tensors. Just a small routing index.

jess: That helps for cache hits by seqlen but watch memory fragmentation. If we keep index only, what's the eviction policy?

aaron: Eviction: two-tier. 1) LRU within seq_bin. 2) Global soft-cap sweep that collapses low-hit bins into a shared cold store.

oliver: How about persistence across driver restarts and model reloads? We can't afford silent staleness.

aaron: Persist metadata + compressed KV tombstones. On restart we do a fast handshake: driver sends model checksum + kernel-priority version; runtime rejects seq_bin-indexed entries if checksum mismatch or kernel-priority ABI changed.

maria: Can we avoid full invalidation on minor kernel selector tweaks? Maybe a compatibility matrix that allows reuse if only order changed but kernels binary-compatible.

aaron: Exactly. We'll version kernel-priority as semantic: major bump = ABI/format change -> full invalidate; minor/patch = reorder/heuristic -> keep and remap. Need a small compatibility table in the driver.

jess: Ran a quick microprofile: seq-binning with index-only cache lookup reduced cache lookup CPU by ~35% for seqlen-heavy traces, but added ~7% memory overhead in metadata.

oliver: 7% seems acceptable. Any perf regressions around batch formation? Batching heuristics might get confused if seq_bins force fragmentation.

aaron: Good point. Batcher will need to be seq-bin aware: prefer coalescing requests inside same bin; allow cross-bin batching only when latency budget allows. New config knobs: `batch_coalesce_threshold` and `cross_bin_timeout_ms`.

maria: Do we have a config sketch?

aaron: Snippet: 
```
seq_bins: [1-32,33-128,129-512]
kernel_priority_versions:
  v1: {ampere: [fused_attn,refmha,fallback]}
cache:
  index_only: true
  bin_eviction: lru
  global_sweep_interval_s: 60
batcher:
  cross_bin_timeout_ms: 5
  coalesce_threshold: 8
```

jess: Can infra-bot run a canary on a single shard with `index_only=true` and `cross_bin_timeout_ms=2`? Want to observe tail latency and GPU utilization.

oliver: @infra-bot can you provision a canary? tag the instance with `seqbin-canary-2026-03` and route 0.5% of traffic.

infra-bot: Provision request received. Creating shard with tags: seqbin-canary-2026-03. Routing rule set to 0.5% traffic. Will post logs when ready. :white_check_mark:

maria: We'll need metrics: per-bin hit rate, index lookup CPU, mem-overhead, cross-bin batch ratio, p99 latency. Also a regression alert if p99 > baseline + 6ms.

aaron: Agree. I'll add dashboards and an eval suite with representative seqlen distribution. Also adding a regression test: reload kernel-priority with minor reorder and ensure handshake keeps cache (no tombstones).

jess: One more: ensure tombstones are small and TTL'd aggressively. We don't want stale keys hanging after model rollback. Proposed `tombstone_ttl_s = 300` and `persistence_epoch` increments on any major model change.

oliver: Sounds good. Next steps: aaron draft PR with config and handshake protocol, jess adds microbench harness, maria defines canary metrics, infra provisions canary.

aaron: I'll open the PR today and ping reviewers. Thanks everyone :rocket:
